why.Sahih Muslim 2643: From Sahih Muslim, on what is written before birth. Cited because it makes assurance harder still.

why.Titus 1:2: God 'cannot lie'. The fixed point the Christian side starts from.
why.Matthew 10:28: Fear not those who kill the body. Why a Christian is not told to hide his faith under threat.

why.Quran 16:106: Excuses one forced to deny the faith while his heart is at rest. The real base of the doctrine.
why.Quran 3:28: Allows guarding yourself among hostile unbelievers. The word here, tuqah, is the root of taqiyya.
why.Sahih Muslim 2605: In Sahih Muslim: the three cases where lying is allowed. War, peace-making, and spouses.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 3030: 'War is deceit', in Bukhari. Often stretched far past what it says, which is battle craft.
why.Jami at-Tirmidhi 1939: From Tirmidhi, below Bukhari in rank. It carries the same three-case list, which is why both appear.

why.John 12:47: Jesus says he does not judge the one who rejects his words. No penalty in this life.
why.John 18:36: 'My kingdom is not of this world', so his servants do not fight. The reason there is no sword.
why.Matthew 13:29-30: Wheat and weeds grow together till harvest. The sorting is left to God, not to a state.
why.Matthew 26:52: 'Put up again thy sword.' Said at the one moment force was to hand.
why.2 Timothy 2:24-26: Tells God's servant to be gentle and patient with opponents, hoping they turn.
why.Quran 9:29: The jizya verse. It commands fighting until the tax is paid, and the dhimmi system rests on it.
why.Quran 5:38: Sets cutting off the hand for theft. One of the hudud penalties named in this case.
why.Quran 9:5: The sword verse. Included because it is read as the high point of coercion.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 6922: 'Whoever changes his religion, kill him.' In Bukhari. The apostasy ruling rests on this.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 6878: In Bukhari: apostasy is one of three grounds on which a Muslim's blood becomes lawful.
why.Sahih Muslim 1690: In Sahih Muslim: the stoning penalty carried out. Stoning is not in the Quran, so it rests here.

why.Acts 17:23-28: Paul starts from a pagan altar to an unknown God. The model this case asks you to follow.
why.Quran 29:61-63: Says that if you ask who made the sun and moon serve you, they answer: Allah. He is not one of them.
why.Quran 41:37: 'Do not prostrate to the sun or the moon.' The Quran forbids the very thing the claim alleges.

why.Quran 15:9: The Quran's own preservation claim. It marks what this case grants: an early text, not a guarded one.

why.Matthew 26:52: 'Put up again thy sword.' The contrast that makes the slogan tempting in the first place.
why.Quran 2:256: 'No compulsion in religion.' Jurists used it against forced conversion, which is why the slogan fails.
why.Quran 9:29: The jizya verse. This is the narrower point that survives: a tax paid 'while they are humbled'.

why.Psalm 19:7: 'The law of the LORD is perfect.' The standard being applied to a law that needed a patch.
why.Quran 4:11: Sets the shares for children and parents. It calls them an obligation from Allah.
why.Quran 4:12: Sets the shares for spouses and for brothers and sisters. The other half of the sum.
why.Quran 4:176: The last verse of the surah, on a man who leaves no child. It adds the sisters' share.
why.Quran 6:114: Says the Book is set out in detail. That claim is what the awl patch sits against.

why.Matthew 7:15-20: 'By their fruits ye shall know them.' The test this case applies, and it is quoted in the text.
why.Matthew 5:44: 'Love your enemies.' Set against what was done to an enemy who had already surrendered.
why.Romans 12:19-21: Tells Christians to leave revenge to God and to overcome evil with good.
why.Quran 33:26-27: The Quran's own account. Some were killed, some taken captive, and their land passed on.
why.Quran 33:21: Calls him an excellent pattern. That is what turns this event into a question.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 3043: In Bukhari: Sa'd's ruling, and Muhammad calling it 'the judgment of Allah'. The core source.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 4028: A second account of the same siege in Bukhari. The event itself is not in doubt.
why.Sunan Abi Dawud 4404: From Abu Dawud. A survivor says the boys were checked for hair to decide who would die.

why.Deuteronomy 18:15-18: The main proof-text. It promises a prophet 'from among your brothers', meaning Israelites.
why.Acts 3:22-26: Peter quotes that promise and applies it to Jesus. The New Testament's own reading of it.
why.John 14:16-17: The Paraclete is 'the Spirit of truth', whom the world cannot see and who will be in them.
why.John 16:7-14: More on the Paraclete. He comes when Jesus goes, and takes what is Christ's to show them.
why.Song of Solomon 5:16: The verse with machamaddim in it. The word is common Hebrew for 'altogether lovely'. It is not a name.
why.Quran 7:157: Says he is written with them in the Torah and Gospel. It assumes those books can be read.
why.Quran 61:6: Says Jesus foretold a messenger named Ahmad. The second claim being tested here.

why.Genesis 17:18-21: Abraham asks for Ishmael. God blesses Ishmael, but sets the lasting covenant with Isaac.
why.Genesis 21:12: 'In Isaac shall thy seed be called.' This is the line the Islamic account has to move.
why.Genesis 22:2: 'Thy son, thine only son Isaac', at Moriah. The verse both sides argue over.
why.Genesis 25:18: Places Ishmael's line from Havilah to Shur, over against Egypt. That is not the Hijaz.
why.Quran 2:125-127: Abraham and Ishmael raise the foundations of the House. The heart of the Islamic account.
why.Quran 3:96-97: Names Bakkah as the first house set up for mankind. Muslims read Bakkah as Mecca.
why.Quran 37:100-107: The near-sacrifice. The son is never named, which is why al-Tabari argued for Isaac.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 3364: In Bukhari: the long account of Hagar and Ishmael at Mecca. Islam's source for the link.

why.Genesis 4:8-16: The Cain and Abel account. No raven, and no line about all mankind. Those come later.
why.Genesis 11:31: Says Abraham came from Ur of the Chaldees. Ur is a place; the fire story grew out of that word.
why.Genesis 15:7: God says he brought Abraham out of Ur. The second verse behind the rabbis' play on words.
why.Quran 5:27-32: The Cain and Abel passage, with the raven and the line about killing all mankind.
why.Quran 18:9-26: The People of the Cave. This is the Seven Sleepers legend, told as history.
why.Quran 21:68-69: Abraham thrown into the fire, and the fire made cool. The third of the three stories.

why.Matthew 22:30: 'In the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage.' The sharpest contrast here.
why.Revelation 21:3-4: God dwells with his people and wipes away every tear. The centre of the Christian hope.
why.Revelation 22:3-5: 'They shall see his face.' The reward stated as God himself, not as things given.
why.Psalm 16:11: 'In thy presence is fulness of joy.' The same hope, said long before.
why.Quran 55:56-74: The maidens 'whom no man or jinn has touched'. The main paradise passage in this case.
why.Quran 56:22-38: Wide-eyed companions. Virgins made of equal age. This is for the companions of the right hand.
why.Quran 78:31-34: Kawa'ib atraban, rendered full-breasted maidens of equal age, with a full cup.
why.Quran 44:51-54: Gardens, silk, and marriage to wide-eyed maidens. A fourth passage with the same picture.
why.Jami at-Tirmidhi 1663: The seventy-two wives report. Tirmidhi ranks below Bukhari, but he graded this one hasan sahih.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 3243: In Bukhari: wives whose marrow shows through the flesh, in a pearl tent sixty miles wide.

why.Genesis 1:27: Male and female are both made in God's image. The starting point of the contrast.
why.Luke 24:9-11: Women are first to report the rising, though such witness carried no legal weight then.
why.Galatians 3:28: 'There is neither male nor female' in Christ. Said of standing before God.
why.Proverbs 31:10-31: Shows a woman buying a field and trading. Useful against the claim that women handled no business.
why.Quran 2:282: The witness rule: two women for one man, 'so that if one errs, the other can remind her'.
why.Quran 4:11: Gives a daughter half a son's share. The inheritance half of this case.
why.Quran 4:34: Calls men the maintainers of women. The Muslim reply builds its answer on this.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 2658: The reason, in Bukhari. Her witness is half 'because of the deficiency of a woman's mind'.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 304: In Bukhari. Women are called lacking in mind and faith. They are also called most of the people of the Fire.

why.Matthew 5:44: 'Love your enemies and pray for them.' The posture set against a line said every day.
why.Romans 10:1: Paul prays that they may be saved. Said of the people he most disagreed with.
why.Quran 1:7: The closing line of the prayer said seventeen times a day. This case is entirely about it.
why.Jami at-Tirmidhi 2954: From Tirmidhi, graded hasan. Here Muhammad names the two groups as Jews and Christians.

why.Luke 1:1-4: Luke names eyewitnesses and earlier accounts, within a lifetime. One end of the comparison.
why.1 Corinthians 15:3-8: A creed handed on within a few years, naming witnesses still alive to ask.
why.2 Peter 1:16: 'We have not followed cunningly devised fables.' A claim to have been there.
why.Quran 16:44: Says the Reminder was sent down so he could make it clear. That is why his words had to be kept.
why.Quran 33:21: Calls him the pattern to follow. It is why hadith reliability carries so much weight for Islam.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 1: The first hadith in Bukhari: deeds are judged by intentions. It points at the collection itself.
why.Sahih Muslim 1: The opening of the other great collection. Both are named because this case is about them.

why.Numbers 30:2: Says a man who swears must not break his word. The rule an annulled oath is read against.
why.Matthew 5:33-37: 'Let your yea be yea.' Jesus on oaths, and why this is about more than one household.
why.Quran 66:1-5: The whole passage. The rebuke, the oath dissolved, and the warning that wives can be replaced.
why.Sunan an-Nasa'i 3959: From Nasa'i, not one of the two Sahih books. Al-Albani graded it sahih. It gives the Mariya occasion.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 4912: In Bukhari: the honey account. Most scholars prefer this, so do not overclaim the other.

why.Matthew 7:15-20: 'By their fruits ye shall know them.' The test this whole part of the site applies.
why.2 Samuel 11:26-27; 12:9: David takes a dead man's wife and God condemns him for it. The Bible judges its own king.
why.1 Thessalonians 4:3-5: Tells Christians to keep from lust and to hold their own bodies in honour.
why.Quran 33:50: Makes captives lawful to the Prophet. The rule the whole episode rests on.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 371: In Bukhari: the marriage consummated on the journey home. The key report in this case.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 4200: In Bukhari: Safiyya first given to Dihya, then given to Muhammad. The captive half of it.

why.Malachi 2:14-15: Calls marriage a covenant with God as witness. The standard a fixed-term deal is measured by.
why.Matthew 19:4-6: 'What God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.' Marriage as lasting by design.
why.Quran 4:24: The verse Shia Islam builds mut'ah on: give them their due for what you have enjoyed.
why.Sahih Muslim 1404: In Sahih Muslim: men on campaign allowed to marry for a set time, even for a garment.
why.Sahih Muslim 1405: In Sahih Muslim: Jabir says it went on into Abu Bakr's reign, until Umar banned it.
why.Sahih Muslim 1406: Cuts against you. In Sahih Muslim it is forbidden 'until the Day of Resurrection'.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 5115: In Bukhari: the ban again. Both sound books record it, so be fair to Sunnis here.

why.John 4:21-24: Jesus says the place stops mattering. Worship in spirit and truth. The contrast with a fixed rite.
why.Acts 17:24-25: God does not live in temples made with hands. The second half of that contrast.
why.Isaiah 44:9-20: The mockery of idol-making. Use it with care: this case says Muslims do not worship the stone.
why.Quran 2:125: Makes the House a place of return and names the station of Abraham. The Muslim origin story.
why.Quran 2:158: Allows the run between Safa and Marwa again. That it had to assumes the older pagan tie.
why.Quran 3:96-97: Names Bakkah as the first house set up, and makes the pilgrimage a duty.
why.Quran 22:26-29: Gives the site to Abraham and orders the circling of the ancient House.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 1597: Umar in Bukhari: 'I know that you are a stone'. Muslims cite it to show the kiss is not worship.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 4287: In Bukhari: the 360 idols cleared out in 630. The shrine's pagan use, from Islam's own record.
why.Jami at-Tirmidhi 877: From Tirmidhi, below Bukhari in rank. It has the stone coming from paradise and speaking at judgment.

why.Matthew 26:52: 'Put up again thy sword', said when force was in reach. One of Jesus's last commands.
why.Matthew 28:18-20: The last command: go and teach. This is the other path the case asks you to compare.
why.2 Corinthians 10:3-4: Says our weapons are not carnal. How the early church read its own mission.
why.Quran 9:5: The sword verse. Kill the idolaters after the sacred months. Late, which is why it counts.
why.Quran 9:29: Fight the People of the Book until they pay the jizya. The part the context answer cannot dissolve.
why.Quran 2:256: 'No compulsion in religion.' Medinan, but earlier, which is why the order decides the reading.
why.Quran 8:39: Fight until there is no strife and religion is all for Allah. The same theme in another surah.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 25: In Bukhari: 'I have been ordered to fight the people until they say' the confession. His own summary.

why.Numbers 23:23: 'There is no enchantment against Jacob.' The rule this report is measured against.
why.Deuteronomy 18:21-22: The prophet test again. It assumes the channel itself can be trusted.
why.1 John 5:18: Says the wicked one does not touch the one born of God. The third piece of the contrast.
why.Quran 25:8: The Quran hotly denies he is 'a bewitched man'. That denial is the internal tension.
why.Quran 17:47: The same charge raised and rejected. Two verses, so it is not a passing remark.
why.Quran 113:1-5: Surah al-Falaq, seeking refuge from those who blow on knots. Muslims tie it to the cure.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 3268: Aisha's report in Bukhari. He imagined he had done a thing he had not done. The core text.
why.Sahih Muslim 2189: The same account in Sahih Muslim. It is as well attested as hadith get, which is the point.

why.1 Peter 2:24: 'He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree.' The mirror image this case is built on.
why.John 1:29: 'The Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.' Substitution offered, not imposed.
why.Isaiah 53:5-6: 'The LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all.' The oldest form of the same idea.
why.2 Corinthians 5:21: Says the sinless one was made sin for us. The exchange, stated most sharply.
why.Quran 53:38: 'No bearer of burdens bears the burden of another.' The verse the Muslim reply must square this with.
why.Quran 6:164: The same rule again. It cuts both ways: Islam does reject transferred guilt, in the Quran.
why.Sahih Muslim 2767a: In Sahih Muslim: a Jew or a Christian given to each Muslim as 'your rescue from Hell-Fire'.
why.Sahih Muslim 2767b: In Sahih Muslim: no Muslim dies but another is put in his place. The sharper wording of the two.

why.Deuteronomy 6:4: The Shema. It is Judaism's core confession, and the reported belief would destroy it.
why.Ezra 7:6-10: Who Ezra was: a scribe skilled in the law of Moses. Nothing in the account hints at more.
why.Nehemiah 8:1-8: Ezra reading the law aloud to the people. The Bible's picture of him is a teacher.
why.Quran 9:30: The verse itself: 'The Jews say Ezra is the son of Allah'. The case is this one line.

why.Genesis 1:1: In every Arabic Bible this verse opens 'In the beginning Allah created'. That settles the word.
why.Mark 15:34: Jesus cries 'Eloi, Eloi' from the cross. That is Aramaic for God, from the same root.
why.Acts 17:23-31: Paul uses a pagan altar's own wording as a bridge. The method this case recommends.
why.Quran 29:46: 'Our God and your God is one.' Muslims press this once you grant the shared word.
why.Quran 112:1-4: The real dispute, and not the word: a God who neither begets nor is born. Argue there.

why.Isaiah 6:1-8: A call scene where God names himself, so the prophet knows who is speaking.
why.Jeremiah 1:4-10: 'The word of the LORD came unto me.' The source is stated, not worked out afterwards.
why.Luke 1:13: The angel's first word to Zacharias is 'Fear not'. That is how these scenes open.
why.Luke 1:26-38: Gabriel names himself to Mary and says who sent him. That is what the cave account lacks.
why.Galatians 1:8: Warns that even an angel from heaven might preach another gospel. Why the question matters.
why.Quran 96:1-5: The first words revealed: Read, in the name of your Lord. The cave passage itself.
why.Quran 74:1-2: 'O you who are wrapped up', told to rise and warn. Read as coming after the terror.
why.Quran 73:1: The other 'wrapped in garments' opening. Both belong to the same early period.

why.Sahih al-Bukhari 6982: The same narration again in Bukhari. It also holds the weak line about the mountain tops.
why.Sahih Muslim 160: The account is in Sahih Muslim too. So the terror and the doubt are in both sound books.

why.John 14:6: 'No man cometh unto the Father, but by me.' One claim, held steadily. That is the contrast.
why.Acts 4:12: 'No other name under heaven' by which we must be saved. The same claim, said by Peter.
why.Hebrews 13:8: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today and for ever. Cited because this case is about a shifting rule.
why.James 1:17: God has no 'variableness, neither shadow of turning'. Quoted in the case for the same reason.
why.Quran 2:62: The open promise to Jews, Christians and Sabians. This is the verse a Muslim friend may quote you.
why.Quran 5:69: The same promise, almost word for word. The repeat is why it is hard to set aside.
why.Quran 3:19: Says the religion with Allah is Islam. The narrowing half of the pair.
why.Quran 3:85: 'Whoever desires other than Islam' will not have it accepted. The verse said to cancel 2:62.
why.Sahih Muslim 153: In Sahih Muslim: a Jew or Christian who hears of him and dies without believing is of the Fire.

why.Exodus 21:2: Release in the seventh year. One of the release rules built into the law of Moses.
why.Exodus 21:16: Death for stealing a man. It outlaws the slave trade at its source.
why.Deuteronomy 23:15-16: A slave who runs is to be sheltered, not sent back. The sharpest break with the ancient world.
why.Philemon 1:15-16: Paul asks for Onesimus back 'no longer as a slave but as a beloved brother'. Quoted in the case.
why.Galatians 3:28: 'Neither bond nor free' in Christ. The line the abolitionists came back to again and again.
why.Quran 4:24: Makes captive women lawful to their captors. The base of concubinage in the law.
why.Quran 33:50: Applies the same rule inside the Prophet's own household.
why.Quran 24:33: The mukataba paper, by which a slave could buy his freedom. The Muslim reply's best verse.
why.Quran 16:71: Speaks of masters and those their right hands possess. It regulates the system rather than ending it.
why.Sahih Muslim 1602: In Sahih Muslim: he buys a slave for two black slaves. Owning and trading, in a sound book.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 2541: In Bukhari: captives taken from Banu Mustaliq. It shows where slaves came from.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 2517: Cuts the other way, and the case says so. In Bukhari, freeing a slave is highly praised.

why.Genesis 1:27: Male and female made in God's image. The ground the Christian objection stands on.
why.1 Corinthians 7:3-5: Paul gives husband and wife an equal claim on each other. Set against a cut made for a husband.
why.Sunan Abi Dawud 5271: The whole textual basis. Abu Dawud himself called it weak and mursal; al-Albani later graded it sound.
why.Sahih Muslim 349: In Sahih Muslim: the bath is due 'when the two circumcised parts meet'. Cited as proof the practice existed.

why.Luke 1:1-4: Luke says he looked into it and wrote. We claim God-breathed meaning through human writers.
why.2 Peter 1:21: Says men spoke as they were moved by the Holy Ghost. The same claim, from the other side.
why.2 Timothy 3:16: 'All scripture is given by inspiration of God.' What is claimed, and what is not claimed.
why.Quran 4:162: Has al-muqimina in one case while the words around it stand in another. The first example.
why.Quran 5:69: Has al-sabi'una in a form inna should not allow. Compare 2:62, where the rule is kept.
why.Quran 20:63: Reads inna hadhani, where the rule calls for hadhayni. The most discussed of the four.
why.Quran 2:177: The praise form again, with al-sabirina. The fourth item on the list.
why.Quran 2:23: The challenge: produce a surah like it. The claim these forms are measured against.
why.Quran 12:2: Calls the Quran clear Arabic. The other half of the claim being tested.

why.Quran 65:4: The verse itself. It sets a waiting period for wives 'who have not yet menstruated'.
why.Quran 33:49: Says there is no waiting period if the marriage was not consummated. That closes the logic.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 5134 (cross-reference:: The Aisha report, here only as a cross-reference. This case holds without it, since the law is in the text.

why.Deuteronomy 22:25-27: Declares the victim innocent: 'to the young woman you shall do nothing'. Quoted in the case.
why.Quran 24:4: The four-witness rule, with eighty lashes for an accuser who cannot meet it.
why.Quran 24:13: Applies the same four-witness test again, in the passage about the slander of Aisha.
why.Quran 24:2: Sets the hundred lashes for zina. That is the penalty the proof rule attaches to.

why.Quran 2:34: 'They prostrated, except Iblis.' That sentence counts him among the angels.
why.Quran 7:11-12: The same scene, plus his reason. He was made from fire, and Adam from clay.
why.Quran 15:30-31: The same exception again. The repeating makes the grammar hard to wave away.
why.Quran 18:50: 'He was of the jinn, so he rebelled.' The verse that pulls the other way.
why.Quran 66:6: Says the angels do not disobey Allah. That is what makes the angel reading costly.
why.Quran 38:73-74: The fifth telling of the same exception. Same wording, same problem.
why.Sahih Muslim 2996 (angels created from l: In Sahih Muslim: angels from light, jinn from fire. It sharpens the question of which one Iblis was.

why.Genesis 1:1-31: The six-day account. Christians read the days in more than one way, but the count is plain.
why.Exodus 20:11: 'In six days the LORD made heaven and earth.' The Bible's total, stated once and left alone.
why.Quran 41:9-12: The itemised list. Two days, then four, then two. This is the arithmetic in question.
why.Quran 7:54: One of the four verses that give the total as six days.
why.Quran 10:3: A second six-day verse. Both are here so you can see the total is not a one-off.
why.Quran 79:27-30: Builds the heaven first, then spreads the earth 'after that'. The second tension in the case.

why.Ezekiel 18:23: Asks whether God has any pleasure in the death of the wicked. The answer given is no.
why.Ezekiel 33:11: 'I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked.' Quoted in the case as the contrast.
why.1 Timothy 2:3-4: Says God would have all men saved. The New Testament half of the same point.
why.2 Peter 3:9: Says he is not willing that any should perish. A second witness to that desire.
why.Deuteronomy 30:19: 'Choose life.' A real command implies a real choice. Quoted in the case.
why.Quran 7:178-179: 'We have created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind', and none can guide whom He leaves astray.
why.Quran 9:51: Says nothing befalls us but what Allah has decreed. The decree stated broadly.
why.Quran 32:13: Says He could have guided every soul, and that He will fill Hell. Both sides quote this one.
why.Quran 76:30: 'You do not will unless Allah wills.' The will itself is placed under the decree.
why.Quran 14:4: Says He leaves astray whom He wills, and guides whom He wills.
why.Quran 81:29: The same line as 76:30, in a short late surah. The repeating is the point.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 6594: In Bukhari: an angel writes the deeds, and whether he is doomed or blessed, before birth.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 6596: In Bukhari, under the heading 'the pen has dried'. The decree is treated as already closed.

why.Matthew 19:8-9: Jesus says divorce was allowed for hardness of heart. No ritual is set as the price of return.
why.Malachi 2:16: God says he hates putting away. The older statement of the same view of marriage.
why.Quran 2:229-230: The divorce rule. After the third time, she is not lawful to him again 'until she has married another husband'.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 5260: In Bukhari: 'not until he tastes your sweetness'. That puts the rule in his own mouth.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 5261: A second telling of the same case in Bukhari. It is why the ruling is not disputed.

why.Quran 9:1: The opening of the one surah with no basmala. Its war footing is part of the Muslim answer.
why.Jami at-Tirmidhi 3086: From Tirmidhi, not one of the two Sahih books, and its grade is disputed. It holds Uthman's own account.

why.Esther 3:1: Where Haman actually appears. The Persian court, about a thousand years after Moses.
why.Genesis 11:3-4: Babel, with baked bricks and a tower to heaven. The other half of the blend.
why.Quran 28:6: Names Haman beside Pharaoh in Egypt. That placing is what the case is about.
why.Quran 28:38: Pharaoh tells Haman to fire bricks and build a tower, to look upon the God of Moses.
why.Quran 40:36-37: The same order to build a tower, told again. Repeating it rules out a slip.
why.Quran 29:39: Lists Pharaoh, Haman and Korah together, which fixes Haman in the time of Moses.

why.Sahih al-Bukhari 3320: In Bukhari: dip the fly in, since one wing carries disease and the other the cure.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 233: In Bukhari: the men of Ukl are told to drink camel milk and camel urine as medicine.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 5686: The same prescription again, in Bukhari's chapters on medicine. Not a stray report.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 5688: In Bukhari: black seed is 'a healing for every disease except death'.

why.Sahih al-Bukhari 3326: The report itself. Adam sixty cubits tall, and people shrinking ever since.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 6227: The same report again in Bukhari. Its standing is not in doubt, which is the whole point.
why.Sahih Muslim 2841: The same in Sahih Muslim. Both of the soundest collections carry it.

why.Sahih al-Bukhari 5134: The report this claim tries to unseat. It is Aisha's own account, in Bukhari.
why.Sahih Muslim 1422: The same account in Sahih Muslim, by other chains. That is why blaming one narrator fails.

why.Quran 2:144: The verse that turns the prayer direction to the Sacred Mosque. The text the claim disputes.

why.Sahih al-Bukhari 1597: Umar's words in Bukhari: 'I know that you are a stone'. It is why the slogan fails at once.

why.Quran 16:106: Excuses one forced to deny the faith. That is leave under threat, not an order to lie.
why.Quran 3:28: Allows care 'unless you fear them'. The fear clause is what the whole rule rests on.
why.Sahih al-Bukhari 3030: 'War is deceit', in Bukhari. The narrow, real thing: battle craft, not daily speech.

why.Quran 56:22-24: The houris in the Quran, with no number given. That absence is the whole point here.
why.Quran 44:54: A second houri verse, again with no count. Check it before repeating the slogan.
why.Jami at-Tirmidhi 1663: Where the number is. Tirmidhi, graded sahih or hasan, and the word is 'wives', not 'virgins'.
